source.description: Base feature commit plus the isolated two-file L-high patch; no other candidate inherited.

notes: Applied request-level laboratory measurements do not replace the original simulated acceptance method.
The original N candidate matrix was completed and failed; it is not unexecuted.
Historical deployed-artifact results have different source/export provenance and are context, not a controlled comparison.
No field Core Web Vitals, INP, physical-device or warm-cache performance proof is claimed.
Raw traces, local machine/account paths, screenshots and isolated patches remain local.

H_H1.classification: Matched mobile measurements after a failed size screen
findings: Only a small homepage LCP change; no consistent guide LCP benefit.
FCP and transferred bytes increased; HTML parsing work increased.
Inline CSS repeats in HTML/RSC and loses independent stylesheet caching. No warm-cache speed penalty was measured.
H remains rejected under the original 5% compressed HTML+CSS growth screen.

I.classification: Offline feasibility only; no candidate or performance run
findings: No substantial dependency-complete safe split established by this bounded investigation.
Absent-class or viewport coverage does not prove unused CSS across interactions/navigation.
This does not prove all selective CSS delivery approaches impossible.

J.classification: Isolated client-data import repair and matched mobile measurements
findings: Approximately 2.3KB initial compressed JavaScript saved without moving bytes into HTML/RSC.
Total emitted JavaScript increased; initial savings are not a net saving across all scripts.
Twelve primary runs did not establish meaningful LCP improvement. Framework code was not labelled removable application code.
Two controlled transport fixtures qualified actual throttled delivery before six website runs.
The measured guide LCP was the existing mobile storm background discovered after blocking CSS, not the separate van photo.
Homepage first paint included substantial initial style/layout work; no large avoidable-JavaScript cause was demonstrated.
This diagnosis did not change original simulated acceptance or establish a homepage repair.

L.classification: Separate matched simulated and applied comparison
findings: Applied guide loading improved but one high-priority observation remained above 2500ms.
Header completion became later and applied TBT increased.
Simulated baseline graph inclusion varied; no robust simulated improvement is claimed.

L1.classification: Independent matched baseline/high/auto comparison, not pooled with L
findings: High priority retained the applied guide benefit but primary simulated guide LCP worsened.
Later header completion and increased applied TBT remain costs.
Auto priority lost the applied benefit. One guide does not establish performance benefit for all fifteen consumers.

M.classification: Retained-trace rendering attribution and two perturbed ownership diagnostics

instrumentedLoads.classification: Instrumented ownership diagnostic; no performance median

instrumentedLoads.classification: Instrumented ownership diagnostic; no performance median

findings: Initial style/layout dominated the retained homepage CSS-to-FCP interval; no forced JavaScript layout loop was demonstrated.
Instrumented ownership loads were substantially perturbed and are not performance medians.
Examined selector/container rules had real consumers; no removal was justified.
